witness.text:

financial_checks.claim: Financial illiteracy costs Americans $246 billion a year, "nearly a thousand dollars per person"
financial_checks.result: Division only was computed: $734 per resident (335M) and $939 per adult (262M). The $246B figure and population inputs are unsourced here.

financial_checks.claim: Cumulative inflation since 2020 about 25%; $100 of groceries is $125
financial_checks.result: FRED CPIAUCSL: 2020 average 258.86; Jan 2026 326.59; +26.2% on all items. The groceries claim uses all-items CPI.

financial_checks.claim: $10,000 in checking for a decade at 2-3% inflation loses "about $2,500"; the bank pays "roughly 10 bucks"
financial_checks.result: Real loss $1,797 (2%), $2,188 (2.5%), $2,559 (3%); at 0.01% the bank pays $1 a year or $10 over ten years.

financial_checks.claim: $200 a month at 8%: from 28 to 65 about $480,000; from 38 about $220,000
financial_checks.result: Monthly: $543,280 and $228,276. End-of-year annual contributions: $487,369 and $209,642. The video's $480,000/$220,000 sit near the annual convention while its later $293,000 and $618,000 use monthly compounding, so conventions are mixed. Gap conclusion holds.

financial_checks.claim: $6,500 at 22%: minimum payments take over 14 years and about $6,500 of interest; debt doubles in about 3 years
financial_checks.result: Schedules use "% of balance plus interest": 1%: 21.4 years, $10,850; 1.75%: 13.8 years, $6,367 (close to the video); 2%: 12.5 years, $5,600. The video's 14 years and $6,500 fit a roughly 1.75% rule that is not stated. Doubling time at 22% is 3.5 years annually and 3.15 years monthly, consistent with "about 3".

financial_checks.claim: Single filer $90,000 less $15,000: tax about $11,500; effective 13-15%; $5,000 raise keeps $3,900
financial_checks.result: $11,414; 12.7% of gross and 15.2% of taxable; 22% marginal gives $1,100 tax and $3,900 kept (federal only).

financial_checks.claim: $300,000 mortgage: 6.5% about $1,900 and 8.5% about $2,300; "nearly $145,000" extra interest
financial_checks.result: $1,896 and $2,307; difference $411 a month; $147,793 over 30 years.

financial_checks.claim: $1,400 repair at 22% over 4 years costs about $2,200
financial_checks.result: A level payment over 48 months totals $2,117. Under "% of balance plus interest" minimums: 1% takes 8.7 years and costs $2,900; 2% 6.2 years and $2,329; 3% 4.9 years and $2,078; $2,200 over 4 years corresponds to a minimum of about 3.5%, so the video's figure is plausible.

Buffett wealth after 50; 59% cannot cover $1,000; 41% and 27% credit myths; term life $20-30; appendectomy $35,000; credit score weights 35/30/15

strengths: Single character gives a clean spine and a natural recap.
One well-placed call to action after delivering value.
weaknesses: Unconditional "never take home less money" is false at benefit cliffs.
Credit-card payoff figures are not reproducible from a stated minimum rule.
Thumbnail states a style, not a stake or the number of concepts.
A promised 401(k) tax-lowering follow-up is never delivered; the character's numbers change between sections.
contradictions: "You will never ever take home less money by earning more" versus the ACA cliff described in the same channel's other videos.
"Almost none of it is your fault" versus ten concepts of individual action.
"pre-tax 401k ... which we'll come back to shortly" is never revisited as a tax-bracket tool.
Sarah's income is $65,000, then $90,000 in the tax example, then $80,000 after the promotion; she has $4,000 in checking yet "doesn't have $1,400 in savings".
improvement_opportunities: Retitle with the count and stake: "10 Money Rules School Skipped (They Cost You $246 Billion)".
Change the thumbnail text to a number from the script ("$246B") or the count ("10 RULES") and use ten small icons or a "1-10" strip.
State the compounding convention on screen and use the monthly figures ($543K versus $228K).
Add "except at benefit cliffs" to the tax-bracket claim and reference the ACA cliff as the exception.
Show the minimum-payment rule used for the credit card example and the resulting schedule.
unavailable: Primary sources for $246 billion, FTC credit-error study, KFF and AAA documents
